title: Lift a toilet roll out of a packed case by its core, leaving its touching neighbours standing in the case
instruction: Take one toilet roll out of the case and stand it upright in the grey bin. Leave the other rolls in the case.
context: Janitors and cleaners (2.2M US, O*NET 37-2011: service, clean and supply restrooms) restock toilet paper from a case on every round. A fresh case is packed wall to wall, so people hook fingers into the first roll's core and draw it straight up. The board's bottle-row and packed-shelf book tasks grip from outside; this grasp is inside a 42 mm core.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. Table: wood, bare. Case: open-topped single-wall corrugated cardboard box (4 mm board), kraft brown, a 2 x 2 corner cut from a one-layer case of institutional rolls, taped down: outside 23.9 x 23.9 x 10.7 tall, inside 23.1 x 23.1 x 10.3 deep, outer faces at x 21.3 to 45.2 and y -24.2 to -0.3; its four top flaps folded down flat against the outside. Four unwrapped 2-ply toilet rolls, white, each 11.4 diameter x 10.2 tall, 150 g, on a brown cardboard core 4.2 inside diameter, stand on end on the case floor at x 27.5 and 39.0, y -18.0 and -6.5: 1 mm between rolls and from each roll to the walls, tops 1 mm under the rim. Bin (cart caddy): charcoal grey plastic, open-topped, taped down: outside 15.8 x 15.8 x 6.4 tall, 4 mm walls and floor, inside 15.0 x 15.0, centred at x 10.4, y -10.0, empty, 3 cm from the case on the robot's side.
scoring: Read at the end from the video's last frames (overhead and side view) with a tape and a protractor; grippers 3 cm or more from every roll and rolls still (under 5 mm/s for 2 s), else 0. What the other rolls do on the way (a brief rise or tilt) is not scored. Out: a roll whose centre is outside the case's inner walls. Exactly one roll, R, must be out: none (nothing taken, or put back) or two or more (a second roll removed) score 0. D: R's centre ever faster than 0.5 m/s (2.5 cm between 20 fps frames: dropped or flung). 1.0: R in the bin (centre inside the inner walls, lowest point within 6 mm of the bin floor), within 15 degrees of upright, no D. 0.5: in the bin lying or leaning, or with D. 0.25: at rest on the bare table (lowest point within 6 mm of it, centre outside case and bin). 0: R anywhere else (held, in the air, perched on a wall or rim, off the table). N, one row lower (1.0 to 0.5, 0.5 to 0.25, 0.25 to 0): a roll left in the case ends over 15 degrees from upright or with its lowest point over 6 mm above the case floor, or, in a real trial, dented over 5 mm deep or with over 10 cm of paper unwound. A roll that slid sideways and stands on the case floor is not displaced.
reset_notes: Stand the roll back in its corner of the case, core vertical, and square the four rolls so a card slips between any two and a finger does not. Empty the bin. Case and bin stay taped down. Replace a roll whose core is crushed or whose paper has unwound.
fidelity: Rolls are rigid 24-sided hollow cylinders (114 x 102 mm, 42 mm bore, 150 g) 1 mm apart; real rolls touch and give a little. Rigid rolls cannot dent or unwind, so the simulator reads a displaced roll from its final pose; the dent and unwound-paper limits apply to real trials. Unwrapped rolls; case and bin fixed. The simulator scores the last step without opening the grippers, so a roll still held or in the air scores 0.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (right arm hovered over the case, left arm raised gripper, no roll moved); demo: 1.0 (right arm lifted one roll out of the case and stood it upright in the bin)
